events.region: Straits of Florida from west end of Seven Mile Bridge to south of Halfmoon Shoal 20 to 60 NM out; Straits of Florida from Halfmoon Shoal to 20 NM west of Dry Tortugas 20 to 60 NM out
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
SMWKEY

The National Weather Service in Key West has issued a

* Special Marine Warning for...
Straits of Florida from west end of Seven Mile Bridge to 20 nm west
of Dry Tortugas 20 to 60 nm out...

* Until 315 AM EST.

* At 215 AM EST, a strong thunderstorm with possible waterspouts was
located 33 nm southwest of Twenty-Eight Foot Shoal Light, moving
east at 5 knots.

HAZARD...Waterspouts and wind gusts 34 knots or greater.

SOURCE...National Weather Service Meteorologist.

IMPACT...Waterspouts can quickly form and capsize boats, cause
considerable damage to vessels and create suddenly higher
waves. Expect wind gusts in excess of 34 knots, suddenly
higher waves, frequent lightning, and heavy downpours.

* The strong thunderstorm will remain over mainly open waters.

events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
* WHAT...Blizzard conditions expected. Total snow accumulations of 1
to 3 inches. Winds will gust as high as 65 mph, reducing visibility
to one quarter mile or less.

* WHERE...Kuskokwim Delta Coast and Nunivak Island.

* WHEN...Until 1 AM AKST Wednesday.

* IMPACTS...Travel could be very difficult. Very strong winds could
cause extensive damage to power lines. Visibilities reduced to one
quarter mile or less due to blowing snow.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...A strong Bering storm arrives at the Southwest
Coast today, bringing gusty southerly winds. Temperatures are
expected to warm Wednesday morning, allowing for a transition to
mixed precipitation.

events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
At 145 am, a large area of strong winds with frequent easterly wind
gusts of 35 to 40 knots blanketed the near and offshore waters gulf
side of the Lower and Marquesas Keys. These winds will spread east
southeastward across the Lower Keys and surrounding nearshore waters
over the next hour, then gradually diminish.

Elsewhere, numerous clusters of showers and a few embedded
thunderstorms were located over the near and offshore waters west of
the Lower Keys. This activity has been moving northward at 15 to 20
knots. The stronger activity will produce wind gusts near 30 knots,
occasional lightning strikes, and blinding downpours. Some of these
cells may rapidly intensify, requiring a Special Marine Warning.
